improvidence

im-PROV-i-dents · noun

Hear It

What It Means

Improvidence is carelessness or lack of foresight, especially with money.

The financial counselor blamed the family's debt on years of improvidence -- spending every paycheck the moment it arrived with no plan for emergencies.

Worked Example

His improvidence in his twenties -- never once opening a savings account -- left him with nothing to fall back on when he lost his job at forty.

Improvidence names the habit itself: spending without any thought for tomorrow, not a single unlucky event.

Compare the words

Synonyms · words with a similar meaning

recklessness: Recklessness is charging into danger with no thought for consequences -- any danger, right now: a dive into dark water, a leap between rooftops. Improvidence is a quieter failure aimed at the future, almost always about money: nothing dramatic happens today, but nothing is set aside for tomorrow.

shortsightedness: Shortsightedness is failing to look ahead -- grabbing today's easy answer and creating next year's problem. Improvidence is shortsightedness in the wallet: the plan for tomorrow is not just weak, it is missing, and the paycheck is gone the day it arrives.

extravagance: Extravagance is spending lavishly -- designer shoes, five-star dinners, more luxury than sense. Improvidence is not about how fancy the spending is: an improvident person may buy only cheap things and still save nothing, because the failure is the missing plan, not the price tags.

What it isn’t · antonyms and near-opposites

thrift: careful management of money

foresight: the ability to plan ahead wisely

Where it sits · how recklessly the future gets ignored — carelessness → improvidence → profligacy

carelessness vs. improvidence: Carelessness is the mild end of the scale that improvidence tops: forgetting a coupon costs a few dollars once, while improvidence is a settled habit of ignoring tomorrow entirely.

profligacy vs. improvidence: Profligacy goes a step beyond improvidence: the improvident person merely fails to save for tomorrow, while the profligate one burns through everything -- money, goods, goodwill -- in a headlong rush toward ruin.

Build the Word

The pieces

prefix — im-

prefix — im-: not (Latin)

root — providence

root — providence: foresight, seeing ahead (Latin (providere))

Put it together

Put it together: im- ("not") + providence ("foresight") = a lack of foresight, especially about money.

Use the root in a new word: provide

Use the root in a new word: provide: The same root survives in the everyday word "provide" -- literally, to see to someone's needs ahead of time.
